> Your computer remembers the answers to recent DNS lookups so it does not have to ask again for every request.

Flushing empties that store, so the next time you visit a site your machine asks a resolver for a fresh answer. That fixes exactly one class of problem: a name whose address has changed while your machine still holds the old one. It does not fix a website being down, a slow connection, or most browser errors, because none of those involve a cached address.

Read the full guide: https://www.kloudbean.com/blog/flush-dns-cache/
